title: The Night Shift Your Brain Never Skips: Cleaning, Filing and Calming After Midnight
title_zh: 你大脑从不缺席的夜班：午夜之后的清理、归档与安抚
intro_zh: 本文约 524 词，从大脑“夜班”的角度讲睡眠如何清理废物、巩固记忆、稳定情绪，含 6 个 CET-4 核心词（flush, tissue, region, consolidate, recall, react），句子难度中等，理解难度约 85%-90%，适合四级阅读训练。

paragraphs.en: At two in the morning your body lies still, but your brain is running a night shift. For decades, sleep looked like a simple off switch to researchers — a quiet state in which not much happened. Modern imaging tells a different story. Across seven or eight hours, the brain washes itself, sorts the day's events and files them away, and some of this work can only be done while you are unconscious.
paragraphs.zh: 凌晨两点，你的身体躺着不动，但你的大脑正在上一个夜班。几十年来，在研究者眼中，睡眠就像一个简单的“关闭开关”——一个安静、没发生多少事的状态。现代成像技术讲述的却是另一个故事。在七八个小时里，大脑给自己“洗澡”，把白天发生的事情分类、归档，而其中有些工作只有在你失去意识时才能完成。

paragraphs.en: One of the busiest jobs is cleaning. In deep sleep, the gaps between brain cells open a little wider, and a watery fluid flushes through the tissue, carrying off waste that piles up during waking hours. Scientists call this the glymphatic system. In a much-cited 2013 study, sleeping mice cleared waste from the brain far faster than mice kept awake. The same cells that work hard all day need a wash at night.
paragraphs.zh: 最繁忙的工作之一是清洁。在深度睡眠中，脑细胞之间的缝隙会略微变宽，一种水状液体冲刷过组织，把清醒时堆积起来的废物带走。科学家把这套系统称为“类淋巴系统”。在 2013 年一项被大量引用的研究中，睡着的老鼠清除脑内废物的速度远远快于被强行保持清醒的老鼠。辛苦工作一整天的那些细胞，夜里需要一次清洗。

paragraphs.en: Cleaning is only half of it. Sleep also decides what you keep. New facts land first in the hippocampus, a small region deep in the brain, where they sit loosely. During slow-wave sleep the hippocampus replays the day to the cortex, which files the important parts away for the long term. Put simply, the brain consolidates what it has learned, and this explains why one good night can do more for an exam than one more hour of reading.
paragraphs.zh: 清洁只是其中一半。睡眠还决定你保留什么。新的知识首先落在海马体——大脑深处一个小小的区域——在那里存放得并不牢固。在慢波睡眠中，海马体会把白天的经历重放给大脑皮层，皮层再把重要的部分长期归档。简单说，大脑会巩固它所学到的东西，这就解释了为什么考前一个安稳的好觉，比再多读一小时书更有用。

paragraphs.en: The numbers are striking. In a classic experiment, students learned pairs of words and then either slept or stayed awake. The sleepers recalled roughly 20 to 40 per cent more the next morning. Brain scans show the sleeping brain repeating the patterns it made while learning, only faster — like a choir practising a song after the teacher has gone home.
paragraphs.zh: 数据很惊人。在一项经典实验中，学生们先学习成对的单词，然后要么去睡觉，要么保持清醒。第二天早上，睡过觉的人能回忆起来的内容大约多出 20% 到 40%。脑部扫描显示，睡着的大脑会重复它学习时形成的那些活动模式，只是速度更快——就像老师回家后合唱团还在练同一首歌。

paragraphs.en: Sleep also steadies feelings. After a sleepless night, the amygdala, the brain's alarm system, reacts almost twice as strongly to upsetting pictures, while the frontal area that usually says wait a moment is quieter. That is why a small problem feels huge at three in the morning and manageable after breakfast. Sleep is not running away from a difficulty; it is a chance to set it down for a while.
paragraphs.zh: 睡眠还能稳定情绪。一夜未眠之后，大脑的警报系统——杏仁核——对令人不安的图片的反应强度几乎翻倍，而那个通常会说“等一下”的前额区域却变得更安静。这就是为什么一个小问题在凌晨三点显得无比巨大，吃完早饭却变得可以应付。睡眠不是逃避困难，而是有机会把它先放下一会儿。

paragraphs.en: Cut sleep short and the price shows up quickly. About one in three adults regularly gets less than seven hours. In lab studies, people limited to four or five hours a night for a week grow slower and less accurate, yet they judge their own performance as almost normal. The brain adjusts to tiredness, and that is exactly what makes short sleep risky.
paragraphs.zh: 削减睡眠，代价很快显现。大约每三个成年人中就有一个经常睡不到七小时。在实验室研究中，每晚只睡四五小时、持续一周的人反应变慢、准确率下降，但他们却认为自己的表现几乎正常。大脑会适应疲倦，而这恰恰是睡眠不足的危险之处。

paragraphs.en: The good news is that the system answers fast. A twenty-minute nap after lunch restores alertness without spoiling the coming night, and a steady bedtime helps the brain begin its shift on time. Bright screens late in the evening send daylight signals that push sleep later, so dimming them an hour before bed is a small and cheap trade.
paragraphs.zh: 好消息是，这套系统反应很快。午饭后小睡二十分钟能恢复警觉，又不会破坏当晚的睡眠；而作息时间稳定，则能帮助大脑准时开始它的夜班。深夜明亮的屏幕会发出“白天”的信号，把睡眠往后推，所以睡前一小时把屏幕调暗，是一笔又小又划算的交易。

paragraphs.en: None of this requires special equipment or expensive apps. Treating sleep as part of the work rather than a break from it is enough, and it costs nothing. Whatever you hope to learn, remember or simply get through tomorrow, the night shift is already on your side.
paragraphs.zh: 这一切都不需要特殊设备或昂贵的应用程序。把睡眠看作工作的一部分而不是工作的中断，就已经足够，而且它不花一分钱。无论你希望明天学会什么、记住什么，或者只是顺利度过，那班夜班都已经站在你这一边。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why people need fewer hours of sleep as they grow older
How the brain cleans, stores and calms itself while we sleep
Why students should read more books before an exam
How to design a quiet and comfortable bedroom
questions.explain: 全文围绕睡眠期间大脑的“夜班”展开：清理废物、巩固记忆、稳定情绪，故 B 正确。A、C、D 均属细节或文中未提。

questions.q: According to paragraph 2, what happens in deep sleep?
options: Brain cells stop working completely for several hours.
The gaps between brain cells widen and fluid carries waste away.
The brain produces more waste than it does during the day.
The hippocampus becomes much larger than usual.
questions.explain: 第二段明确指出深度睡眠时脑细胞间隙略微变宽，水状液体冲刷组织带走废物，故选 B。A 与“大脑在上夜班”矛盾；C、D 文中无依据。

questions.q: Why is short sleep especially risky, according to paragraph 6?
options: Because tired people find it hard to fall asleep at night.
Because people get used to the tiredness and do not notice how much worse they perform.
Because a week of short sleep always leads to serious illness.
Because the brain stops cleaning itself after only a few days.
questions.explain: 第六段说睡眠受限者表现变差，却自认为“几乎正常”，大脑适应了疲倦，这正是危险所在，故选 B。A、C、D 均属过度推断或文中未提。

questions.q: The word "consolidate" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to
questions.explain: 第三段讲海马体把信息交给皮层长期归档，consolidate 意为“巩固、加强并储存”，故选 B。A 意思相反，C、D 与语境不符。
